Sample Size Planning for the Standardized Mean Difference (AIPE)

Source: R/ss_aipe_smd.R
ss_aipe_smd.Rd

Determines the per-group sample size needed for a two-independent-groups design so that the confidence interval for the population standardized mean difference, denoted \(\delta\), is no wider than a user-specified value when the sample standardized mean difference (Cohen's d) equals \(\delta\). This is the accuracy in parameter estimation (AIPE) approach of Kelley and Rausch (2006), the standardized mean difference companion to power-based planning via ss_power_smd. Optionally, supplying assurance returns the smallest sample size, not below the plan without it, at which the realized interval is no wider than the target with at least that probability, computed exactly.

Usage

ss_aipe_smd(
  true_smd,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  width,
  assurance = NULL,
  assurance_method = "analytic"
)

Arguments

true_smd

The supposed value of the population standardized mean difference \(\delta\) the sample size is planned against: a value the researcher posits, either a minimally important effect or a value believed to be true in the population, never a sample estimate. Echoed in the returned table as the true_smd row.

conf_level

Desired confidence level (i.e., \(1-\alpha\), where \(\alpha\) is the Type I error rate). Default 0.95. A level above .999999998, whose tail areas are below 1e-9, is refused (see "Small tail areas" in ci_nc_t).

width

Desired (full) width of the two-sided confidence interval on \(\delta\).

assurance

Optional probability with which the realized confidence interval is to be no wider than width. When NULL (the default), the plan is for the width of the interval at \(d = \delta\); when supplied (e.g., 0.80, 0.90, 0.99), the function returns the smallest per-group sample size, not below that plan, at which the probability that the realized interval is no wider than width is at least assurance (see Details). Must be NULL or strictly between 0.50 and 1. An assurance above .999999998 is refused with a condition of class dmar_argument_invalid: the floor of 1e-9 on a tail area (see "Small tail areas" in ci_nc_t) applies to (1 - assurance) / 2.

assurance_method

How the probability that the realized interval is no wider than width is found, used only with assurance. Only "analytic" (the default) is offered here: the probability is computed exactly, and the plan is the smallest sample size, not below the plan without assurance, at which it reaches assurance. "simulation", which ss_aipe_sc_ancova, ss_aipe_reg_coef with noncentral = TRUE, and ss_aipe_src offer, where the probability has no exact form, is refused with a condition of class dmar_argument_invalid, whether or not assurance is given, since a simulated estimate of an exact probability would only add Monte Carlo error.

Value

A data.frame with columns term and value:

necessary_n_per_group

the necessary per-group sample size.

true_smd, width

the planning inputs, so the assumptions the sample size was planned under travel with the result. The true_smd row is the supposed effect the plan is built on, as given (with its sign): a value the researcher posits, either a minimally important effect or a value believed to be true in the population, never a sample estimate.

assurance

the requested probability; present only when assurance was given.

assurance_attained

the exact probability, at necessary_n_per_group and true_smd, that the realized interval is no wider than width, at least assurance; present only when assurance was given.

The confidence level is reported in the printed footer, and with assurance the footer names the assurance method; the attribute assurance_method records it, and assurance_probability records that assurance_attained is "exact".

Details

The plan without assurance. The interval is the one ci_smd reports: the confidence interval for the noncentrality parameter of the noncentral t distribution, with \(2n - 2\) degrees of freedom, at the observed t statistic, rescaled to \(\delta\) by \(\sqrt{2/n}\), with n the per-group sample size. The function uses \(\delta\) as if it were d and returns the smallest n at which that interval is no wider than width (Kelley & Rausch, 2006, pp. 371–372). The width depends on \(\delta\) only through \(|\delta|\).

The assurance step. At a given n the width of the interval depends on the sample only through d and grows as \(|d|\) grows, so the realized interval is no wider than the target exactly when \(|d| \le d^*(n)\), the value of \(|d|\) at which the width equals the target. With \(\lambda = |\delta| \sqrt{n/2}\), \(\nu = 2n - 2\), and \(t^* = d^*(n) \sqrt{n/2}\), the probability of that event under normality with equal variances is $$P_n \;=\; \int_0^\infty \Big\{ \Phi\big(t^* \sqrt{v/\nu} - \lambda\big) - \Phi\big(-t^* \sqrt{v/\nu} - \lambda\big) \Big\}\, f_\nu(v)\, dv,$$ where \(\Phi\) is the standard normal distribution function and \(f_\nu\) the density of a chi square on \(\nu\) degrees of freedom: the t statistic is \((Z + \lambda) / \sqrt{V/\nu}\) with \(Z\) standard normal and \(V\) chi square, independent. The integral involves only the normal distribution and the chi square, so it does not depend on R's noncentral t, which is a normal approximation above a noncentrality of 37.62. It depends on \(\delta\) only through \(|\delta|\), and the plan is the same for true_smd and -true_smd.

The returned sample size is the smallest n at or above the plan without assurance, \(n_0\), at which \(P_n\) is at least assurance (assurance_method = "analytic"), found by doubling a step upward from \(n_0\) and then bisecting, and assurance_attained is \(P_n\) there. The search assumes that \(P_n\) does not decrease as n grows from \(n_0\). In 45 planning sets (\(|\delta|\) of 0, .2, .5, 1, and 2, widths of .25, .5, and 1, and assurances of .80, .90, and .99) it did not decrease at any n from \(n_0\) to ten past the plan, and the plan was the smallest n found by raising n one at a time from \(n_0\). Because the width changes little with d, \(P_n\) rises steeply with n: at true_smd = .5 and a width of .5 it is .838 at 129 and .916 at 130.

The probability was checked against the noncentral t distribution computed by R's pt() where it is exact, against a second integral that conditions on the normal variate instead of the chi square, and against the proportion of intervals no wider than the target among samples of two groups of normal data.

Large noncentrality. R's pt() is a normal approximation to the noncentral t distribution above a noncentrality of 37.62, and its series loses accuracy above 33 with more than 2,000 degrees of freedom, ranges that narrow targets with a large \(|\delta|\) reach (true_smd = 2 with a width of .25, or true_smd = 1 with a width of .1). The interval ci_smd reports is computed exactly there (see ci_nc_t), so the width of the interval increases with \(|d|\) at every sample size, the event above is \(|d| \le d^*(n)\), and \(P_n\) is exact.

The published procedure. Kelley and Rausch (2006, pp. 372–374) plan with assurance as follows: at \(n_0\), find the value \(\delta_\gamma\) that \(|d|\) exceeds with probability \(1 - \gamma\), where \(\gamma\) is assurance, by searching between the upper limit of a one-sided interval and the upper limit of a two-sided interval computed at \(d = \delta\) (their Equations 25 to 31), and plan for \(\delta_\gamma\) as for \(\delta\). The procedure does not compute \(P_n\). Since \(\delta_\gamma\) is found at \(n_0\) and the plan for it is larger, that plan can be larger than the smallest sample size that attains the request: in the 45 sets above it attained the request in every set and was one case larger in 7, all but one at an assurance of .99; at true_smd = 1, a width of .5, and an assurance of .99 it is 150, where \(P_n\) is .9943, and this function's plan is 149, where it is .9903. It can also fall short: at true_smd = 0, a width of .8, and an assurance of .95 it is 49 per group, where \(P_n\) is .9499, and this function's plan is 50, where it is .9946.

Warning

The returned value is the sample size per group.

Examples

ss_aipe_smd(true_smd = .5, conf_level = .95, width = .30)
#>  term                  value
#>  necessary_n_per_group 353  
#>  true_smd              0.500
#>  width                 0.300
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

# With assurance the last row is the exact probability, at the planned
# sample size, that the interval is no wider than the target.
ss_aipe_smd(true_smd = .5, conf_level = .95, width = .30, assurance = .8)
#>  term                  value
#>  necessary_n_per_group 356  
#>  true_smd              0.500
#>  width                 0.300
#>  assurance             0.800
#>  assurance_attained    0.860
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
#> 
#> Assurance method: analytic; assurance_attained is the exact probability that the interval is no wider than the width
ss_aipe_smd(true_smd = .5, conf_level = .95, width = .30, assurance = .95)
#>  term                  value
#>  necessary_n_per_group 359  
#>  true_smd              0.500
#>  width                 0.300
#>  assurance             0.950
#>  assurance_attained    0.966
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
#> 
#> Assurance method: analytic; assurance_attained is the exact probability that the interval is no wider than the width

# Reversing the groups reverses the sign of the effect and leaves the
# plan unchanged.
ss_aipe_smd(true_smd = -.5, conf_level = .95, width = .30, assurance = .95)
#>  term                  value 
#>  necessary_n_per_group 359   
#>  true_smd              -0.500
#>  width                 0.300 
#>  assurance             0.950 
#>  assurance_attained    0.966 
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
#> 
#> Assurance method: analytic; assurance_attained is the exact probability that the interval is no wider than the width
